ei.title: Doing Good for Its Own Sake
ei.subject: 9월_2026 고2 모의고사
ei.lesson: Doing Good for Its Own Sake

fullPassage: Our adult brains retain a preference for perpetuating good, fair behavior. Simply perceiving ourselves as people who do good deeds and behaving accordingly motivates us to do greater good in the future. In one paid study of one hundred college students, subjects who wrote down a list of past good deeds and were then asked to donate money to a charity gave, on average, over half the earnings they’d made from the study — almost twice as much as those who had been instructed to recall previous bad deeds. In addition, subjects who’d taken pains to describe not only how they’d been nice to others but how people responded were likely to donate significantly less than those who focused purely on the actions themselves. In other words, people who seemed concerned about appearances (e.g., the impact of their good deed, as much as the deed itself) were less generous than those who cared more about doing good for its own sake.

questions.passage: Our adult brains (A)[retain / abandon] a preference for perpetuating good, fair behavior. Simply perceiving ourselves as people who do good deeds and behaving accordingly (B)[motivates / discourages] us to do greater good in the future. In one paid study of one hundred college students, subjects who wrote down a list of past good deeds and were then asked to donate money to a charity gave, on average, over half the earnings they’d made from the study — almost twice as much as those who had been instructed to recall previous bad deeds. In addition, subjects who’d taken pains to describe not only how they’d been nice to others but how people responded were likely to donate significantly less than those who focused purely on the actions themselves. In other words, people who seemed concerned about appearances (e.g., the impact of their good deed, as much as the deed itself) were less (C)[selfish / generous] than those who cared more about doing good for its own sake.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: (A) retain=유지하다, (B) motivates=동기를 부여하다, (C) generous=관대한. 우리 뇌는 선행 성향을 유지하고, 선행이 더 큰 선행의 동기가 되며, 선행 자체를 중시한 사람이 더 관대했다.
det.analysis:
❌ ① abandon(버리다) - motivates - generous: (A) abandon은 '버리다'로, 성향을 '유지한다(retain)'는 문맥에 반대
❌ ② retain - discourages(단념시키다) - generous: (B) discourages는 '단념시키다'로, 선행을 '동기부여한다'는 문맥에 반대
❌ ③ retain - motivates - selfish(이기적인): (C) selfish는 '이기적인'으로, 더 '관대했다(generous)'는 문맥에 반대
✅ ④ retain - motivates - generous: 원문 일치 ←정답

questions.passage: Our adult brains retain a preference for (A)[perpetuating / ending] good, fair behavior. Simply perceiving ourselves as people who do good deeds and behaving accordingly motivates us to do greater good in the future. In one paid study of one hundred college students, subjects who wrote down a list of past good deeds and were then asked to donate money to a charity gave, on average, over half the earnings they’d made from the study — almost twice as much as those who had been instructed to (B)[recall / forget] previous bad deeds. In addition, subjects who’d taken pains to describe not only how they’d been nice to others but how people responded were likely to donate significantly less than those who focused purely on the actions themselves. In other words, people who seemed (C)[indifferent / concerned] about appearances (e.g., the impact of their good deed, as much as the deed itself) were less generous than those who cared more about doing good for its own sake.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: (A) perpetuating=지속시키는, (B) recall=회상하다, (C) concerned=신경 쓰는. 선행을 지속시키려는 성향, 과거 나쁜 행동을 회상하라는 지시, 겉모습을 신경 쓰는 사람들이라는 문맥.
det.analysis:
❌ ① ending(끝내는) - recall - concerned: (A) ending은 '끝내는'으로, 좋은 행동을 '지속시킨다'는 문맥에 반대
✅ ② perpetuating - recall - concerned: 원문 일치 ←정답
❌ ③ perpetuating - forget(잊다) - concerned: (B) forget은 '잊다'로, 과거 행동을 '회상하라'는 문맥에 반대
❌ ④ perpetuating - recall - indifferent(무관심한): (C) indifferent는 '무관심한'으로, 겉모습에 '신경 쓰는' 사람이라는 문맥에 반대

questions.passage: Our adult brains retain a preference for perpetuating good, fair behavior. Simply (A)[perceiving / ignoring] ourselves as people who do good deeds and behaving accordingly motivates us to do greater good in the future. In one paid study of one hundred college students, subjects who wrote down a list of past good deeds and were then asked to (B)[donate / withhold] money to a charity gave, on average, over half the earnings they’d made from the study — almost twice as much as those who had been instructed to recall previous bad deeds. In addition, subjects who’d taken pains to describe not only how they’d been nice to others but how people (C)[ignored / responded] were likely to donate significantly less than those who focused purely on the actions themselves. In other words, people who seemed concerned about appearances (e.g., the impact of their good deed, as much as the deed itself) were less generous than those who cared more about doing good for its own sake.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: (A) perceiving=인식하는, (B) donate=기부하다, (C) responded=반응했다. 자신을 선한 사람으로 인식하고, 돈을 기부하며, 사람들이 어떻게 반응했는지를 묘사했다는 문맥.
det.analysis:
❌ ① ignoring(무시하는) - donate - responded: (A) ignoring은 '무시하는'으로, 자신을 선한 사람으로 '인식한다'는 문맥에 반대
❌ ② perceiving - withhold(주지 않다) - responded: (B) withhold는 '주지 않다'로, 돈을 '기부한다'는 문맥에 반대
✅ ③ perceiving - donate - responded: 원문 일치 ←정답
❌ ④ perceiving - donate - ignored(무시했다): (C) ignored는 '무시했다'로, 사람들이 어떻게 '반응했는지'라는 문맥에 반대

questions.passage: Our adult brains ①<u>retain</u> a preference for perpetuating good, fair behavior. Simply ②<u>perceiving</u> ourselves as people who do good deeds and behaving accordingly motivates us to do greater good in the future. In one paid study of one hundred college students, subjects who wrote down a list of past good deeds and were then asked to donate money to a charity gave, on average, over half the earnings they’d made from the study — almost twice as much as those who had been instructed to recall previous bad deeds. In addition, subjects who’d taken pains to describe not only how they’d been ③<u>rude</u> to others but how people responded were likely to donate significantly less than those who focused purely on the actions themselves. In other words, people who seemed concerned about appearances (e.g., the impact of their good deed, as much as the deed itself) were less ④<u>generous</u> than those who cared more about doing good for its own sake.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: rude(무례한)는 nice(친절한)의 반의어
det.analysis:
❌ ① retain - 우리 뇌가 선행 성향을 유지한다. 원문 적절
❌ ② perceiving - 자신을 선한 사람으로 인식한다. 원문 적절
✅ ③ rude - 원문 nice. 자신이 타인에게 얼마나 '친절했는지' 묘사했다는 맥락 ←정답
❌ ④ generous - 선행 자체를 중시한 사람이 더 관대했다. 원문 적절
det.tip: been nice to others(타인에게 친절했다) vs rude(무례한)

questions.passage: Our adult brains retain a preference for ①<u>perpetuating</u> good, fair behavior. Simply perceiving ourselves as people who do good deeds and behaving accordingly motivates us to do greater good in the future. In one paid study of one hundred college students, subjects who wrote down a list of past good deeds and were then asked to donate money to a charity gave, on average, over half the earnings they’d made from the study — almost twice as much as those who had been instructed to recall previous ②<u>good</u> deeds. In addition, subjects who’d taken pains to describe not only how they’d been nice to others but how people ③<u>responded</u> were likely to donate significantly less than those who focused purely on the actions themselves. In other words, people who seemed ④<u>concerned</u> about appearances (e.g., the impact of their good deed, as much as the deed itself) were less generous than those who cared more about doing good for its own sake.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: good(좋은)은 bad(나쁜)의 반의어. 비교 대상 집단은 과거 '나쁜' 행동을 회상한 사람들이어야 대조가 성립
det.analysis:
❌ ① perpetuating - 좋고 공정한 행동을 지속시키려는 성향. 원문 적절
✅ ② good - 원문 bad. 선행을 적은 집단과 '나쁜' 행동을 회상한 집단을 대조하는 맥락 ←정답
❌ ③ responded - 사람들이 어떻게 반응했는지. 원문 적절
❌ ④ concerned - 겉모습을 신경 쓰는 사람들. 원문 적절
det.tip: recall previous bad deeds(과거의 나쁜 행동을 회상하다) vs good(좋은)

In addition, subjects who’d taken pains to describe not only how they’d been nice to others but how people responded were likely to donate significantly less than those who focused purely on the actions themselves. In other words, people who seemed concerned about appearances (e.g., the impact of their good deed, as much as the deed itself) were less generous than those who cared ④<u>less</u> about doing good for its own sake.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: less(덜)는 more(더)의 반의어. 선행 자체를 중시한 사람이 더 관대했으므로 '더(more)' 신경 썼다가 맞음
det.analysis:
❌ ① motivates - 선행이 더 큰 선행의 동기가 된다. 원문 적절
❌ ② donate - 자선단체에 돈을 기부한다. 원문 적절
❌ ③ recall - 과거의 나쁜 행동을 회상하다. 원문 적절
✅ ④ less - 원문 more. 더 관대했던 사람들은 선행 자체를 '더(more)' 중시했다는 맥락 ←정답
det.tip: cared more about doing good(선행을 더 중시했다) vs less(덜)

det.korean: 미래(future)에 더 큰 선행을 하도록 동기를 부여한다

det.tip: do greater good in the ______ → future(미래)

det.analysis:
❌ ① (A): 만들다 - (B): 벌다: 두 의미가 반대로 배치됨
✅ ② (A): 벌다 - (B): 만들다: (A)는 '돈을 벌다', (B)는 '만들다'로 정확 ←정답
❌ ③ (A): 벌다 - (B): 벌다: (B)는 파이를 '만들다'
❌ ④ (A): 만들다 - (B): 만들다: (A)는 돈을 '벌다'
det.tip: make money = (돈을) 벌다 / make a pie = 만들다

questions.stem: 다음 영영 정의에 해당하는 단어로 가장 적절한 것은? "a piece of research that examines a subject or question in detail"

det.korean: 연구: 어떤 주제나 질문을 상세히 조사하는 연구 활동
det.analysis:
✅ ① study: 연구. 정의에 정확히 부합 ←정답
❌ ② lecture: 강의. 조사 활동이 아님
❌ ③ contest: 대회. 정의와 무관
❌ ④ ceremony: 의식, 행사. 정의와 무관
det.tip: study = a piece of research examining a subject in detail

questions.passage: Our adult brains retain a __________ (prefer) for perpetuating good, fair behavior. Simply perceiving ourselves as people who do good deeds and behaving accordingly motivates us to do greater good in the future.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (1단어) (영어로)

det.korean: 명사형. prefer → preference
det.analysis: prefer(동사: 선호하다)를 명사형 preference(선호, 성향)로 변환. 관사 a 뒤, for 앞에 명사가 필요하다.

questions.passage: In addition, subjects who’d taken pains to describe not only how they’d been nice to others but how people responded were likely to donate significantly less than those who focused purely on the actions themselves. In other words, people who seemed concerned about __________ (appear) were less generous than those who cared more about doing good for its own sake.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (1단어) (영어로)

det.korean: 명사형(복수). appear → appearances
det.analysis: appear(동사: 나타나다)를 명사형 appearances(겉모습, 외관)로 변환. 전치사 about 뒤에 명사가 필요하며, 여기서는 '남에게 보이는 겉모습'을 뜻하므로 복수형 appearances로 쓴다.

questions.passage: Our adult brains retain a preference for perpetuating good, fair behavior. Simply perceiving ourselves as people who do good deeds and behaving accordingly motivates us to do greater good in the future. In one paid study of one hundred college students, subjects who wrote down a list of past good deeds and were then asked to donate money to a charity gave, on average, over half the earnings they’d made from the study — almost twice as much as those who had been instructed to recall previous bad deeds. In addition, subjects who’d taken pains to describe not only how they’d been nice to others but how people responded were likely to donate significantly less than those who focused purely on __________. In other words, people who seemed concerned about appearances (e.g., the impact of their good deed, as much as the deed itself) were less generous than those who cared more about doing good for its own sake.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 행동 그 자체(the actions themselves)에 순수하게 집중한 사람들
det.analysis:
❌ ① other people's praise(타인의 칭찬): 겉모습·평판을 신경 쓴 쪽에 가까워 반대 방향
❌ ② their own feelings(자신의 감정): 본문에 근거 없음
✅ ③ the actions themselves: 남의 반응·겉모습이 아니라 '행동 그 자체'에 집중했다는 맥락 ←정답
❌ ④ the final results(최종 결과): 본문에 언급되지 않은 표현
det.tip: focused purely on ______ → the actions themselves(행동 그 자체)

questions.passage: Our adult brains retain a preference for perpetuating good, fair behavior. Simply perceiving ourselves as people who do good deeds and behaving accordingly motivates us to do greater good in the future. In one paid study of one hundred college students, subjects who wrote down a list of past good deeds and were then asked to donate money to a charity gave, on average, over half the earnings they’d made from the study — almost twice as much as those who had been instructed to recall previous bad deeds. In addition, subjects who’d taken pains to describe not only how they’d been nice to others but how people responded were likely to donate significantly less than those who focused purely on the actions themselves. In other words, people who seemed concerned about appearances (e.g., the impact of their good deed, as much as the deed itself) were less generous than those who cared more about doing good __________.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 선행 그 자체를 위해(for its own sake) 선을 행하는 것을 더 중시한 사람들
det.analysis:
❌ ① for public praise(대중의 칭찬을 위해): 겉모습을 신경 쓴 쪽으로 오히려 덜 관대했던 집단
❌ ② with great effort(큰 노력을 들여): 본문 주제(동기)와 초점이 다름
✅ ③ for its own sake: 남의 평가가 아니라 선행 '그 자체를 위해' 선을 행하는 것을 중시했다는 맥락 ←정답
❌ ④ in secret ways(은밀한 방식으로): 본문에 근거 없음
det.tip: doing good ______ → for its own sake(그 자체를 위해)
